### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4ff1a025fa4568505bfbc66a0f8cbeb3bab06ff`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4ff1a025fa4568505bfbc66a0f8cbeb3bab06ff` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `836aa42fed621198f540cf29c777854f0a1899be` — the merge of head `e354975f300ac10ad1b71754caddd94d70503fb2` into base `d4ff1a025fa4568505bfbc66a0f8cbeb3bab06ff`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 836aa42fed621198f540cf29c777854f0a1899be && git checkout 836aa42fed621198f540cf29c777854f0a1899be
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d4ff1a025fa4568505bfbc66a0f8cbeb3bab06ff e354975f300ac10ad1b71754caddd94d70503fb2 && git checkout -B drift-repro d4ff1a025fa4568505bfbc66a0f8cbeb3bab06ff && git merge --no-ff e354975f300ac10ad1b71754caddd94d70503fb2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4ff1a025fa4568505bfbc66a0f8cbeb3bab06ff
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d4ff1a025fa4568505bfbc66a0f8cbeb3bab06ff` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `68ff23949d4291e0cc5485a893a8a7f0506f0480`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/empty-projection-door.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-empty-projection-refusal.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/query-expression-conformance.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/unprojected-read-declared-fields-conformance.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/declared-read-columns.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-query-validation.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts, packages/spec/src/data/projection-names-a-field.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts

Written 2026-10-29T12:07Z. Read-only: card #27165 (body and all three comments: triage 6466016076, claim 6488430651, dev report 6495887715), PR #27541 body and file list, `git diff origin/main...68ff2394` (merge-base `f57eddcf`, origin/main at `aef631b8`), the cited code in `/home/claude/os-main-ro`, and the head's check-runs. Face: `narrowing` (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset; no published schema, no governed path in the file list), so the scope floor is every path of the diff outside prose.

**Check-runs on the head, read 2026-10-29T11:57Z:** 46 runs — 22 `success` (Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, three scoped lints, Type Check · source gates, · consumer gates, · debt ledger, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected, Plan Test Core shards, Test UI, Auto Label, filter), 14 `skipped` (UI, docs, live-E2E and opt-in lanes), 10 `in_progress` with no conclusion yet (Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check · workspace). No failure read. The queue guard reads "every check green" on its own; this record does not stand in for the ten still running.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set narrowing at `ObjectQL.find` / `findOne` (`@objectstack/objectql`).** A non-empty `fields` list whose every entry the object's field map lacks (after `PLATFORM_PROVISIONED_COLUMNS` = `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at` are admitted) is refused with `status: 400`, `code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR'`, before any driver read; on `main` it fell back to `ast.fields = undefined` and the driver answered every column. **Right** — it is the ruling's words (6466016076: "a projection that is empty after dropping unknown columns is an empty projection, so it is refused with #27008's refusal"), and the diff reuses `refuseEmptyProjection` rather than adding a second refusal, as the claim required.
- **The #7589 tolerance for a mixed projection is kept.** `['nope', 'title']` still projects `{ title }` on both verbs (engine.ts: `filtered` non-empty takes the old path; pinned by the CONTROL case and the two surviving `[#7589 GUARD]` cases). **Right.**
- **`fields: []`, absent or `null` `fields`, and a registry-less object are unchanged.** `assertProjectionNamesAField` still runs at entry; the filter block is still guarded by the same three-part condition (a field map present, `fields` an array, and non-empty). **Right.**
- **No public-surface change.** `refuseProjectionOfUnknownColumns` is a new named export of `empty-projection-door.ts`, but that module is not re-exported from `packages/objectql/src/index.ts` and no other package imports it (read: index.ts, repo-wide import grep); `refuseEmptyProjection` stays module-private, its new fourth parameter defaults to `[]` so the #27008 message is byte-identical (`got []`). No type, option key or wire shape moves. **Right.**
- **No REST change.** The REST door refuses the same request earlier, at `assertProjectionFieldsExist` (`protocol-query-validation.ts`, `400 INVALID_FIELD`), so no wire caller reaches the new branch; `mapDataError`'s declared-status passthrough serves the engine's `status`/`code` unchanged to a host that surfaces engine errors. **Right.**
- **`expand` is unchanged.** `expandRelatedRecords` (engine.ts ~12790) forwards `nestedAST.fields` and appends `'id'` when the caller did not name it, so a nested all-unknown projection reaches the sub-read as `['nope', 'id']`, filters to `['id']`, is never empty, and expands to `{}` after the #7537 strip. The door file's new docblock paragraph claims exactly this and the code bears it out. **Right.**
- **`count` and `aggregate` are untouched.** The unknown-plain filter exists only at the two `find` / `findOne` sites (`known.has(f)` appears twice in engine.ts, both changed here). **Right.**
- **Engine-internal callers cannot trip it.** Every `this.find` / `this.findOne` in engine.ts that names `fields` names `id` (organization probe, autonumber seed, reference check, relation-filter site) or passes none; the `summaryKeyColumns` read is a `driver.find`. The flow `get_record` node's `findOne` arm appends `id` (`projectionNamingId`); its `find` arm forwards the authored list, so a flow whose `fields` are all typos now gets the node's structured refusal (`refusalCarriedBy`) instead of every column — the ruling's intent. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/27165-engine-all-unknown-projection-refused.md`: `'@objectstack/objectql': patch`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, the **BREAKING** banner, the ADR-0087 disposition (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), Before / Now / Unchanged / Who sees it / remedy. Under ruling A as mechanised in `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` ("the level follows the metadata protocol alone … a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and its ADR-0087 disposition"), a `none` declaration must grade every entry `patch`: **the level matches the diff.** No authorable key, default or enum moves (no `packages/spec` path in the file list), so `Metadata-protocol: none` is true. The declaration is the same shape, level and disposition as the landed #27008 changeset (`9fa70b4a25`), which this PR extends. The `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line is on the PR body and the changeset alike; Check Changeset concluded `success`. **Right.** The `Skills-docs:` line owes a follow-up (see ③).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **(a) REST `select ['nope']` answers `400 INVALID_FIELD`; in-process `fields ['nope']` answers `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`.** Answered, not escalated. The two doors never both answer one request: the REST door refuses at `assertProjectionFieldsExist` before the engine is called, so a wire caller sees only `INVALID_FIELD`, and an in-process caller sees only the engine's code. The engine's code is the ruling's explicit choice (6466016076 names #27008's refusal, which carries `VALIDATION_ERROR` as the HTTP doors' `select: []` does); the card body's `INVALID_FIELD` was option A, which triage did not pick. The status agrees (400). Within the engine the dotted-projection door uses `INVALID_FIELD` and this one `VALIDATION_ERROR`; that is a pre-existing split the ruling knowingly left, and the dev's "not decided here" is the right account. Nothing for this PR to change; a seat wanting one code across both doors files a triage question, not a fix here.
- **(b) PR #27477 (draft) edits engine.ts near the imports and both filter sites; #27339 near the imports.** Answered. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 68ff2394` is clean; engine.ts moved on `main` since the merge-base in five hunks (imports, ~15423, ~17143, ~17462, ~20165), none inside the two filter blocks. Order of landing is the seats' procedure ("whichever lands later merges `main`"), not a defect in this tree.
- **(c) `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — content/docs/data-modeling/queries.mdx`.** Stands as a follow-up the seat carries: that file is outside the claim's file surface (6488430651), the #27008 landing already added the empty-projection sentence there, and this narrowing adds one more. Not a landing blocker for the engine change; the seat files or carries it, as the report says.
- **Dev deviations.** Two extra objectql test files edited (they pinned the fallback; inside "their tests under `packages/objectql`"); no assignees / reviewers per the coordinator's rule; report marker under the stamp line; dogfood run twice. All within the claim.
- **`open_questions: []`** — none to answer.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged against the cited code on `main` and the scenario the card accepts: a narrower request is never answered wider; an empty projection is refused, never read as every column; the mixed tolerance stays.

- **`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`** — holds. Both sites keep the three-part guard, compute `known` from the field map plus `PLATFORM_PROVISIONED_COLUMNS` (one list, `declared-read-columns.ts`), and refuse only when `filtered.length === 0`; `ast.fields = filtered` is equivalent to the old non-empty branch. The `requested` list handed to the message is `ast.fields` after planning, and I checked whether planning can make it differ from the caller's own list: `planFormulaProjection` rewrites only when a formula field is named and then adds `id` plus every stored column (never empty), `withFileOwnerKey` only adds `id`, `expandSearchOnAst` touches `where` not `fields`, `fillQueryAstDefaults` does not touch `fields` — so whenever the branch fires, `got […]` names exactly what the caller wrote. Refusal position (after the dotted door, the orderBy door and `requireFindOnePredicate`) matches the sibling doors; it cannot sit at entry because it needs the registry's field map. Probed: `fields: ['created_at']` (provisioned only) still reads; `fields: ['mailing_street']` (a retired, stored-but-undeclared column) is now refused rather than silently reading the default projection — consistent with the rule, and the driver is never asked; a list of only non-string entries (the retired field-node object form) empties and is refused with the objects printed in `got`, where before it read every column.
- **`packages/objectql/src/empty-projection-door.ts`** — holds. Same function, same `status`/`code`/`param`/`object` fields, the declaration's words still read off `EngineQueryOptionsSchema.fields` (`PROJECTION_NAMES_NO_FIELD`, `packages/spec/src/data/projection-names-a-field.ts`), default `requested = []` keeps the #27008 text byte-identical. The thin export is `: never` and is called in a statement position in both sites, so control cannot fall through. The docblock's `expand` claim is true (see ①).
- **`packages/objectql/src/engine-empty-projection-refusal.test.ts`** — holds. Real `ObjectQL`, exact-projecting driver double that counts reads, `wireAnswer` through `mapDataError`; the two refusal cases assert status, code, the declaration's words, `got ["nope","nada"]` / `got ["nope"]` and zero driver reads; the CONTROL covers both verbs. Red-on-main is credible: the old code never threw here.
- **`packages/objectql/src/query-expression-conformance.test.ts`** — holds. The one `[#7589 GUARD]` pin that said "a future tighten cannot ride in … without meeting its own ruling" is replaced by a `[#27165]` pin that cites the ruling that met it; the mixed-projection guards for `find` and `findOne` stay as written, so the tolerance the #7589 ruling kept is still pinned.
- **`packages/objectql/src/unprojected-read-declared-fields-conformance.test.ts`** — holds. Across all three driver shapes the retired-only projection is now a refusal; dropping `expectNoRetiredColumn` there is correct because no row is served and no driver read happens, so the retired column cannot leak.

**Should-fix (not a FAIL).** Field-map checkability. The engine's filter condition is `_findSchema?.fields` truthy, so an object whose registered `fields` is an empty record (or, for a host that bypasses the spec, an array) gets `known` = the three provisioned columns and every real name is "unknown": on `main` that case fell back to every column; on this head it is refused with a message that asserts "none of them is a field of X", which is not a true verdict when the map is simply unreadable. `declaredColumnSet` in the same package and `resolveQueryFields` at the REST door both answer "no opinion" for an absent, array or empty map. I grade it should-fix rather than must-fix because `ObjectSchema.fields` is a record and `applySystemFields` injects the owner/tenant/audit columns into nearly every map, so no in-repo object reaches it; a follow-up could build `known` from `declaredColumnSet(_findSchema)` and skip the filter when it returns `undefined`, so both doors share one checkability rule.

No must-fix found.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published spec and the cited code on `origin/main`:

- `EngineQueryOptionsSchema.fields` (`data-engine.zod.ts` L110-112, `PROJECTION_ACCEPT_SET`) declares "at least one field name; a value naming no field … is refused". `['nope']` passes that schema, and on the old `main` the #7589 tolerance emptied it in the engine, so a projection the spec says must name a field reached the driver naming none and was answered as every declared column. The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real at the point where the list actually empties, with one refusal, one set of words and the existing #27008 door. On that axis the design is **sound**.
- Tried to break it: (a) planner-rewritten lists cannot empty and cannot mis-name (① 3); (b) expand sub-reads never reach the arm (① 8); (c) registry-less hosts untouched (① 6); (d) `findOne` ordering — `requireFindOnePredicate`, the orderBy door and the dotted refusal still run first, so no shape refused before is answered now; (e) `beforeFind` hooks run inside `executeWithMiddleware` after the filter, so no hook can be handed the fallback; (f) system-context reads are refused like every caller, as for #27008; (g) the ADR-0144 hunks `main` added between the heads touch `insert`, `update` and `aggregate` only. Nothing widened, nothing silently changed.
- Consumer axis: through REST nothing moves (the ingress refuses the name first). The only consumers that lose a behaviour are in-process callers naming only columns the object lacks, which the census (278 call texts) found none of, and `expand` sub-reads are structurally exempt. The code half holds.
